items.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: Now I never heard Louis Armstrong do a tribute to anybody. His great tribute was to carry the music on.

ctx.x: Yeah, the music of. Now I never heard Louis Armstrong do a tribute to anybody. His great tribute was to carry the music on. When you listen to Louis Armstrong you heard those who preceded him. He didn’t turn his back on the future and face the past to give validity to music. This music is only validified and further advanced in its credibility by those who look forward and constantly advance the music, you know, and build on top of what has already happened.
